mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a significant short-term discount rate tightening, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening events are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS spike is not clearly distinguishable from noise.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 60-day forward returns during similar inflation spikes are not statistically worse than during stable inflation (p > 0.05), or the CPIAUCSL jump is not confirmed by labor market data.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of more than 50,000 jobs in a month coincides with investor optimism about economic recovery, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In analogous labor expansion episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during contractionary periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) show consecutive monthly gains exceeding +3% and +2% respectively, it signals robust supply-side momentum that supports higher equity valuations, yielding positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > +3% AND INDPRO > +2% in consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 100 such dual-gain episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three consecutive months indicates tight labor markets, which typically precedes equity risk-on flows and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In comparable tightening episodes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a month while HOUST remains flat, it signals weakening demand-side momentum and a higher probability of equity drawdowns, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -5% AND HOUST >= 0 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during similar supply-side weakness episodes are not statistically worse than during expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 6-month decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) suggests a loss of momentum in economic activity, which tends to precede risk-off flows and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during comparable slow-downs are not statistically lower than during robust growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) rises by more than 10% in a month and PAYEMS exceeds 120,000, it reflects strong consumer and labor market confidence, which typically drives risk-on equity flows and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +10% AND PAYEMS > +120,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during analogous confidence events are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).
